sources.entry: PhotoMiner - macOS app for finding and lost forgotten photos on your disks.

summary.one_liner: PhotoMiner is a macOS app that scans chosen directories for photographs and displays them chronologically, grouped by month and year.
summary.what_it_does: The app scans a directory you select, drop onto the window, or drop onto the dock icon, and collects the pictures it finds. It orders them by the date taken from EXIF data, falling back to file creation time when EXIF is missing. Photos are grouped so each month of each year has its own group containing only photos taken in that month. From the app you can open photos in their default application (mostly Preview), view them with QuickView, remove them, make basic modifications, or reveal them in Finder. You can select photos and drag them into a new directory to copy them there. The README describes no other features.
use_cases: find forgotten photos scattered across disks
sort an unorganized folder of pictures by date
browse old photo memories by month and year
copy selected photos into a new folder
review photos with QuickView on a Mac
how_to_run: Install PhotoMiner as a macOS application (the README links an AppStore entry, but the link is blank)
Select a directory, or drag it onto the application window or dock icon
Select photos and drag them to a new directory to copy them
notable: Orders photos by EXIF date taken, falling back to file creation time
Groups photos into one group per month of each year
Drag-and-drop a folder onto the window or dock icon to scan it
Opens photos in the default app, QuickView, or Finder
